clips.send: A mountain can tower above you or fade into layers across the horizon. If you could frame just one view, what would you want someone to notice first?

clips.send: Liúbái is space left open on purpose. In Fan Kuan’s painting the pale gap between the mountain and the foreground reads like mist. That sense of quiet depth is part of the painting’s yìjìng, the mood and imagined world it creates.

clips.send: In linear perspective, a set of parallel lines receding into the scene can appear to meet at one vanishing point. A shan-shui handscroll often combines shifting viewpoints (sǎndiǎn tòushì), so your eye can travel as the scroll opens.

clips.send: Shan-shui (shānshuǐ, “mountains and water”) is a Chinese tradition of painting landscapes. Northern Song painter Guo Xi described three ways to look into a landscape. Change the viewpoint and trace the path your eyes take.

clips.send: 留白是有意留下的空处。范宽画中，山脚与前景之间的淡处像一层雾。虚实相间，让人感到山谷幽深，这就是画面营造意境的一种方式。

clips.send: 线性透视中，向画面深处延伸的一组平行线，看起来会汇向同一个消失点。山水长卷常以散点透视组织景物，展开时能看到不同视角的景物，仿佛一路游览。
